extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment analysts, hospital financial officers, and stakeholders commenting on IPPS/LTCH proposed rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and methodologies for calculating FY2027 inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) and LTCH payment components including wage index treatment (rural floor, imputed floor, 5% cap, transition exceptions), outlier payment qualification and thresholds, reconciliation adjustments, and related budget neutrality adjustment factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of §412.103 reclassification hospitals in rural wage index calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with FY 2025, include hospitals with §412.103 reclassification along with geographically rural hospitals in all rural wage index calculations; only exclude 'dual reclass' hospitals (hospitals with simultaneous §412.103 and MGCRB reclassifications) in accordance with the hold harmless provision at section 1886(d)(8)(C)(ii) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with prior policy, beginning with FY 2024, data of all §412.103 hospitals (including those that have an MGCRB reclassification) are included in calculation of the rural floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to calculate national rural floor budget neutrality adjustment factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use FY 2025 discharge data to simulate payments and post-reclassified national wage indexes and compare national simulated payments without the rural floor to national simulated payments with the rural floor to determine the budget neutrality adjustment factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the determined national adjustment to the national wage indexes to produce rural floor budget neutral wage indexes; summary table provided elsewhere in rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of ARPA imputed floor (minimum area wage index) and non-budget-neutral treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 9831 of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (amending section 1886(d)(3)(E)), the imputed floor for hospitals in all-urban States is required for discharges on/after Oct 1, 2021 and shall not be applied in a budget neutral manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the imputed floor after application of the rural floor and do not apply reductions to the standardized amount or to the wage index to fund the increase in payments to hospitals in all-urban States resulting from the imputed floor; see section III.G.2 for full discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent 5-percent cap policy on wage index decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital's wage index shall not be less than 95 percent of its final wage index for the prior fiscal year (a 5-percent cap on any decrease), regardless of the cause of decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The permanent cap policy is applied in a budget neutral manner through an adjustment to the standardized amount so estimated aggregate payments under the cap equal what they would have been without the cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to calculate wage index cap budget neutrality adjustment factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use FY 2025 discharge data to simulate payments and compare aggregate payments without the 5-percent cap to aggregate payments with the 5-percent cap, using proposed FY2027 labor-related share percentages and proposed FY2027 relative weights, and applying proxy hospital readmissions and VBP payment adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resulting comparison determines the wage index cap budget neutrality adjustment factor for FY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional payment exceptions for discontinuation of low wage index hospital policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary transition policies established for hospitals significantly impacted by discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy using authority under section 1886(d)(5)(I) of the Act; FY2025 transitional exception equaled additional FY2025 amount if FY2025 wage index were 95% of FY2024; FY2026 transitional exception equaled additional FY2026 amount if FY2026 wage index were 90.25% of FY2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027, propose to extend the transitional exception for hospitals continuing to experience large decreases, using authority twice (narrow transitional exception and applying it budget neutrally). See prior IFC and final rules for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to calculate transition wage index budget neutrality adjustment factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use FY 2025 discharge data to simulate payments and compare aggregate payments without the transition (and with the 5-percent cap) to aggregate payments with the proposed transition (and with the 5-percent cap), using proposed FY2027 labor-related shares and relative weights, and applying proxy hospital readmissions and VBP payment adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the resulting proposed FY2027 budget neutrality adjustment factor to the standardized amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier payment qualification and definition of fixed-loss cost threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for outlier payments, a case must have costs greater than the sum of the prospective payment rate for the MS-DRG plus IME and DSH payments, uncompensated care payments, supplemental payments for eligible IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals, any new technology add-on payments, and the outlier threshold (fixed-loss amount). This sum is the outlier 'fixed-loss cost threshold.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hospital's cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) is applied to total covered charges to convert charges to estimated costs; eligible cases receive payments based on a marginal cost factor applied to estimated costs above the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginal cost factors for outlier payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The marginal cost factor for FY2027 is 80 percent for most DRGs and 90 percent for designated burn MS-DRGs (927, 928, 929, 933, 934, 935).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS has historically used 90% for designated burn DRGs (since FY1989) and 80% for other DRGs (since FY1995).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory outlier target range and method to compute percent target
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with section 1886(d)(5)(A)(iv) of the Act, outlier payments for any year are projected to be not less than 5 percent nor more than 6 percent of total operating DRG payments plus outlier payments. When setting the outlier threshold, compute the percent target by dividing total projected operating outlier payments by total projected operating DRG payments plus projected operating outlier payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses this percent target when determining the outlier threshold; operating outlier target affects the standardized amount via an outlier offset factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of IME and DSH from outlier target and not requiring Medicare Advantage IME
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include IME and DSH payments within the outlier target amount; therefore, it is not necessary to include Medicare Advantage IME payments in the outlier threshold calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1886(d)(3)(B) requires reducing the average standardized amount by a factor to account for the estimated total of outlier payments as a proportion of total DRG payments (excluding IME/DSH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cost report CCRs and MAC referral criteria for outlier reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlier reconciliation at cost report settlement is based on operating and capital CCRs computed from the relevant cost report and charge data determined at the time the cost report is settled (42 CFR 412.84(i)(4)). MACs are instructed to identify cost reports for CMS approval of outlier reconciliation based on specified criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original criteria (CR 13566 context): (1) actual operating CCR fluctuates ±10 percentage points or more compared to interim CCR used at billing, and (2) total operating and capital outlier payments for hospital exceeded $500,000 for that cost reporting period. New criteria (CR 14233): (1) actual operating CCR is ±20% or more from the operating CCR used for claim payment, and (2) total operating and capital outlier payments > $500,000; additionally, hospitals in their first cost reporting period are referred regardless of CCR change or outlier payment amount. If reconciliation is approved, reconcile both operating and capital outlier payments. See Claims Processing Manual section 20.1.2.5 for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-step methodology to incorporate projected outlier reconciliations (operating)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 5-step method: Step 1 identify hospital cost reports meeting original (1a) or new (1b) criteria; Step 2 determine aggregate amount of operating outlier reconciliation dollars (under original and new criteria); Step 3 calculate aggregate total Federal operating payments across applicable hospitals using cost report data; Step 4 compute percentage of total operating outlier reconciliation dollars to total Federal operating payments for the cost report year; Step 5 adjust the outlier target using the Step 4 percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS advances historical data by 1 year using cost reports on a six-year lag (most recent complete data). The Step 4 percentage when rounded can be negative or positive, affecting the outlier threshold (negative reduces threshold, positive increases it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data selection and anomaly handling in projecting outlier reconciliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically advance historical cost report data by 1 year using a 6-year lag (e.g., use FY2019 for FY2025). To estimate effects of new reconciliation criteria, apply new criteria to historical cost reports as if in effect. If most recent data produce anomalous results (e.g., Step 4 percentage rounds to +0.0% inconsistent with historical negative percentages), hold the data constant and use the percentage from a prior final rule (e.g., use FY2019-based percentage from FY2025 final rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FY2021 cost reports produced a Step 4 ratio of +0.0% (($457,535 / $77,326,439,126) × 100) which was considered anomalous compared to historical negative ratios; CMS proposed using the FY2019-based ratio of −0.041994% from the FY2025 final rule for FY2027 modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed FY2027 operating outlier target and standardized amount offset
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2027, propose to target an outlier threshold at 5.14 percent [5.1 percent - (−0.04 percent)] to incorporate the projection of outlier reconciliation dollars; proposed operating outlier offset to the standardized amount is 0.949 (1 − 0.051).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will evaluate updated data (e.g., March 2026 HCRIS extract) in developing the final rule and may change approach if updated data do not show anomaly; public comments invited on methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-step methodology to incorporate capital outlier reconciliation payments (capital Federal rate adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 5-step method analogous to operating reconciliation: Step 1 identify cost reports meeting original (1a) or new (1b) criteria; Step 2 determine aggregate amount of capital outlier reconciliation dollars (under both criteria); Step 3 calculate aggregate total capital Federal payments across applicable hospitals; Step 4 compute percentage of total capital outlier reconciliation dollars to total capital Federal payments; Step 5 adjust the capital outlier adjustment factor using the Step 4 percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reconciliation dollars are only available on cost reports and not in MedPAR claims data, in Step 5 the capital reconciliation percentage from Step 4 is added to the estimated percentage of capital outlier payments otherwise determined using the shared threshold (addition for capital vs subtraction for operating). The unified shared threshold identifies outlier cases for both operating and capital payments; difference in step application stems from that sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of capital outlier reconciliation dollars on capital Federal rate
rubrics_metrics.description: When aggregate capital outlier reconciliation dollars in Step 2 are negative, the estimate of capital outlier payments is lower than the estimate using the shared threshold, producing a relatively smaller outlier budget neutrality adjustment factor and an increase to the capital Federal rate; when aggregate capital outlier reconciliation dollars are positive, the estimate is higher producing a relatively larger adjustment factor and a decrease to the capital Federal rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors and contrasts with the operating reconciliation effect, and is incorporated into the capital Federal rate adjustment via Step 5.
